chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan from Sa'id al-A'raj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who has a water share (shirb) with a group of people in a canal that has partners, and some of them become independent of their share. Can he sell his share? He said: 'Yes, if he wishes he sells it for silver, and if he wishes he sells it by measure of wheat.'

key_terms.الشِّرْبُ: Water share or right to draw water from a source
key_terms.كَيْلِ حِنْطَةٍ: Measure of wheat (a commodity-based pricing method)
key_terms.وَرِقٍ: Silver (used here as a standard for currency/value)

ai.seo_question: Can a partner sell their share of water in a shared canal according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the transferability of water rights (*shirb*) within a shared irrigation system, affirming that a partner may sell their share to others. The Imam’s allowance of payment in either silver (*waraq*) or wheat (*hinta*) highlights the flexibility of consideration in Islamic commercial law, accommodating both monetary and barter transactions. This ruling underscores the principle that water shares are treated as distinct, tradable assets (*mal*) within the framework of joint ownership.
